lead: 3x Semiconductor ETF / SOXL — triple leverage on the peace rally
smaller: Virgin Galactic / SPCE — the $450,000 ticket relaunches the dream
Roblox / RBLX — the metaverse playground misses its bookings
Airbnb / ABNB — revenge travel gets its receipts
why_lead: The dominant crowd narrative of 15 February is the relief rally after Russia said it had begun a partial troop pullback (CNBC [[n1497]], Guardian [[n1496]], BBC [[n1503]], Putin to Scholz [[n1320]]), and the most leveraged retail vehicle moved most: SOXL +16.22% to 46.01 USD, still -17.81% over 20 sessions, against S&P 500 +1.58%, Nasdaq 100 +2.47%, SOX +5.47%, VIX -9.28%, WTI -3.55%. Chips had their own concrete catalysts published 14–15 February (AMD closing Xilinx [[n0687]], AMD passing Intel's market value [[n0781]], Intel buying Tower [[n0851]]; NVDA +9.18%), the Yahoo Finance geopolitical-shock piece [[n1179]] anchors the analog, and the Smart Money View has a genuine split (NATO caution, Euronews scepticism, Fed and liquidity worries, Bloomberg's crash hedge). Relation to strictly earlier retail notes: 2022-02-09 ran Nvidia as a smaller item with SOXL as the leveraged expression of the Arm-deal relief. This lead is a material update with a different catalyst (the claimed pullback plus the AMD/Intel deals) and only evidence published on 14–15 February; the 9 February leverage-decay caution is not repeated, and the invalidation is the unverified pullback. The 14 and 15 February war-hedge items (GDX, USO) are the trades this rally unwound.
why_smaller: Virgin Galactic / SPCE: the largest single-stock move on the card (+31.94% to 10.74 USD) with a clean own-date catalyst ($450,000 tickets, Forbes [[n0920]]; company release [[n0919]]) and a sympathetic move in Joby (+26.89%, ANA partnership [[n0852]]); the space/future lottery-ticket narrative has not appeared in earlier retail notes.

Roblox / RBLX: the metaverse pure play bought into its print (+7.29%, +13.77% over five sessions) and then hit by disappointing bookings and a big after-hours drop on 15 February (Reuters [[n0883]], Business Journals [[n0880]]); a sell-the-news narrative distinct from the other three. Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-03 ran Meta as 'the metaverse bill comes due'; this is a different company and a new results catalyst.

Airbnb / ABNB: the reopening comeback with a fresh beat-and-guide (CNBC [[n0784]], Al Jazeera [[n0785]]) and a 16.41% 20-session run, with Marriott's rebound [[n1208]] as confirmation; no earlier retail note covered travel.
considered_not_chosen: Crypto (BTC +4.67% to 44,575.20 USD, ETH +8.40%, COIN +7.02%, MARA +12.05%): crypto led on 8, 14 and 15 February; the relief bounce adds no new crowd catalyst, so it appears neither as lead nor as a smaller item.

AMC and GameStop (+9.75%, +7.75%): AMC was a 9 and 14 February smaller item; used only as card values in the lead's Social Signal. AMC's Evanston theatre acquisition (n0780) is another expansion headline of the kind already covered.
Joby Aviation / JOBY (+26.89%): folded into the Virgin Galactic item as the same future-mobility lottery ticket.
Bloom Energy and Plug Power (+13.82%, +10.71%): high-beta relief moves without an own-date company catalyst.
Upstart (+4.31%; results 15 February after the close): no own-date results headline in the window, so the outcome is not described.
Avoided: n1326 (Reuters LIVE MARKETS 'S&P 500 futures weigh Russia relief vs PPI pop'), a rolling live blog, not used for the PPI outcome; no Duma-appeal headline was used.
